_about: The Guild of Shadows chain's dialogue (owner 2026-10-09: upstream offered "[Traveler's]" and said nothing else), and the classic quests' period lines, names and class words (quest entry scan 2026-10-11: the line that offers a quest's first keyword, and the names and plain words upstream's generator replaced with <Player>, such as Wariel's [name] in "What is your [name]?"; and, class-word scan 2026-10-11, the class the guides' authors were called by and the guides' placeholders for it, as <Class>, the player's class, with New Crest's accept keyword the row's own class; every other character is upstream's). deploy/bin/quest_dialogue.py writes it into the DataQuest rows at every start; "step" is a key of epic_chains_data.json "steps" (one quest ID per class), "ids" plain quest IDs that get the same text ("name" is for the reader); a value is one text for every class, an object by class (a step only), or a list with one entry per stage. "guard": the digests of the values a row may hold for the fix to change it (upstream's after epic-chains-v1, then each earlier version of this file). Chat lines are in deploy/hearthdaoc-quests.json.

Description.Infiltrator: <Player>. Supplies are desperately needed at the Keep on the road to Snowdonia, else our comrades there will suffer dearly. They wait in Humberton; collect them and take them to our allies in need. It is a small [errand], but small errands are how the Guild learns whom it can trust.
Description.Mercenary: <Player>. It seems our allies have got a little problem with getting much-needed supplies to the Keep on the road to Snowdonia. Who better than a sell-sword like us to deliver the goods? It's a small [errand]. Do it well, and there will be bigger ones.
Description.Cabalist: <Player>. Our allies at the Keep on the road to Snowdonia are short of supplies, and a bundle waits for them in Humberton. Not every problem is solved with a construct; this one needs someone to carry it down a road. Will you run this [errand] for the Guild?
Description.Necromancer: <Player>. The Temple has friends at the Keep on the road to Snowdonia, and they are short of supplies. A bundle waits for them in Humberton. It is a small [errand], but Arawn watches how his servants carry small things before he trusts them with great ones.
Description.Reaver: <Player>. Our friends at the Keep on the road to Snowdonia are short of supplies, and today the Temple needs a courier, not a killer. A bundle waits in Humberton. A small [errand], but the Temple remembers who can be trusted with small things.

SourceText: Good. Go to Humberton and find Bline; he waits near the bindstone. He will give you the supplies and tell you where to go. Do not linger on the road.
Talk to Thol Dunnin on your way to Snowdonia. She's the smith at Snowdonia Station, up in the Black Mountains; she'll tell you where they go from there.
Keep going down the road and deliver the supplies to Ley Manton at Swanton Keep. I'd go with you myself, but I can't leave my post.
StepText: Collect the supplies from Bline, who waits near the bindstone in Humberton.
Talk to the smith Thol Dunnin at Snowdonia Station.
Deliver the supplies to Ley Manton at Swanton Keep.
TargetText: Camelot sent you? Then these are yours to carry. Bundled and ready, just as they came to me.
From Bline? Good. The Keep has been waiting for these.
Supplies from Camelot? Hand them here.
set.FinishText: All here, and just in time. Our friends in Camelot keep their word, and so, it seems, do you. Take this for your trouble, <Player>.

set.Description: <Player>, you are new to these isles, and new eyes see what old ones miss. Strange things have been coming up out of the water near Aanniogel, and the folk there are frightened. Tage knows more of it than I do. Will you look into these [strange] happenings for us?

SourceText.Infiltrator: Then speak with Tage. He stands beneath the stones beside Carys, the necromancer trainer.
SourceText.Mercenary: Then speak with Tage. He stands beneath the stones beside Carys, the necromancer trainer.

SourceText.Necromancer: Then speak with Tage. He stands beneath the stones, just beside me.

SourceText: Kimmy Glaze sells bolts in Aanniogel, north of here. She has seen these creatures with her own eyes. Go to her.
They come up in the shallows south-east of here. Destroy two of them, and perhaps the rest will keep to the deep.
One more, and the shallows should be quiet.

SourceText.Infiltrator: Adam Glaze, the shield merchant inside the gates of Caer Gothwaite, keeps watch for Elaru. He will want to know.

StepText: Speak to Tage, beneath the stones beside Carys in Caer Gothwaite.
Find Kimmy Glaze, the bolt merchant in Aanniogel.
Destroy two lesser water elementals in the shallows south-east of Aanniogel. (1/2)
Destroy two lesser water elementals in the shallows south-east of Aanniogel. (2/2)
Report to Adam Glaze, the shield merchant inside the gates of Caer Gothwaite.

TargetText.Infiltrator: Elaru sent you? Then listen. Something has been coming up out of the water near Aanniogel. The fisherfolk call them strange beings, and no two of them tell the same tale.

TargetText: You've come about the things in the water? Thank the gods. They're water elementals, small ones, but they've torn two nets to pieces and nearly drowned a boy.
The lesser water elemental collapses into a spray of cold, foul water.
The second elemental spills away into the shallows and does not rise again.

FinishText.Infiltrator: Two of them, back into the water for good? Elaru chose well. Those creatures don't rise on their own; something stirs them, and we will learn what in time. Take this, with Elaru's thanks.

Description.Infiltrator: <Player>. Word of your first errand has come back to me, and it was good. Captain Dillon, who keeps the guard tower near Ludlow, has a problem he would rather the Guild solve quietly than the Defenders solve loudly. Will you go to [Captain Dillon]?
Description.Mercenary: <Player>. Word is you can be trusted with an errand. Now let's see you trusted with a sword. Captain Dillon, who keeps the guard tower near Ludlow, has two of his own guards turned thief, and he doesn't want the Defenders crowing about it. Will you go to [Captain Dillon]?
Description.Cabalist: <Player>. You have shown you can be trusted. Captain Dillon, who keeps the guard tower near Ludlow, has lost something old and valuable, and he would rather the Guild recover it quietly than the Defenders recover it loudly. Will you go to [Captain Dillon]?
Description.Necromancer: <Player>. You were swift and silent; our friends noticed. Now the Temple has a debt to collect. Captain Dillon, who keeps the guard tower near Ludlow, needs help he cannot ask of the Defenders, and a soldier who owes the Temple a favour is worth more than gold. Will you go to [Captain Dillon]?
Description.Reaver: <Player>. You've run your errands; now you get to swing that flail. Captain Dillon, who keeps the guard tower near Ludlow, has two of his guards turned thief and loose in the Black Mountains. A soldier who owes the Temple a favour is worth more than gold. Will you go to [Captain Dillon]?

SourceText: Then go to the guard tower near Ludlow. Mind your manners; he is a soldier, and soldiers don't love our kind.

They were seen heading north, for the red dwarf camp where the shaman keeps her fire. Each of them carries one of the stones. Bring them back. What happens to the thieves is your affair, and I won't ask.
Agisthil can't be far; he was making for the same camp. He'll have the other one.
Two rough halves of one stone. Omis, the gemcutter at Swanton Keep, can make something of them.
There. Cut, polished and set together: a crediac once more. Only a crediac can put Brodic down, and now you carry one. He haunts the southern Black Mountains.
Captain Dillon will want to hear of it.
StepText: Speak with Captain Dillon in the guard tower near Ludlow.
Find the thief Frund at the red dwarf camp north of Captain Dillon's tower, and take his stone.
Find the thief Agisthil at the same camp and take his stone.
Take both stones to Omis, the gemcutter at Swanton Keep.
Rid the land of Brodic in the southern Black Mountains; only the Crediac can defeat him.
Return to Captain Dillon with what is left of the Crediac.
TargetText: So they send me a <Class>. Fine; I'm in no position to be choosy. A monster named Brodic has been terrorizing the land, a dead thing that won't stay down, and only a crediac stone can defeat him. Two of my own guards, Frund and Agisthil, turned thief and made off with the stones.
Frund falls. In his pouch is a Crediac stone: half of a broken stone, rough and unworked.
Agisthil falls, and you take the other Crediac stone from his belt.
Crediac stones? Let me see them. Both of them, mind; half a stone is no use to anyone.
Brodic falls, and the crediac cracks in your pouch, its work done.
Brodic is gone? Then show me what's left of the crediac.

FinishText.Infiltrator: Cracked clean through; it did its work. Brodic is gone, and the thieves with him. I didn't think the Guild would see it done so cleanly. Take this, <Class>, and tell your master that Dillon pays his debts.

set.Description: <Player>. Word of you has reached even these isles. I have a task that needs a quiet hand. A man named Martley has been selling what he hears in Caer Gothwaite to whoever pays, and he has fled to a camp in the wilds. Adam Glaze has what you need. Will you work in the [shadows] for us?
SourceText: Then go to Adam Glaze, the shield merchant inside the gates. He will give you a cloak and tell you where Martley hides.
He hides at the camp with a single tent, north-west of here, among the Nypholites. Wear the cloak; it may buy you a few steps before they know you for a stranger.
Take Martley's body back to Adam Glaze in Caer Gothwaite.
That's the end of him. Take this package to Tage, beneath the stones by Carys. He'll know what to do with it, and he'll see you're rewarded.
StepText: Speak to Adam Glaze, the shield merchant inside the gates of Caer Gothwaite.
Slay Martley at the single-tent camp north-west of Caer Gothwaite.
Bring Martley's body to Adam Glaze.
Take Adam Glaze's package to Tage.

TargetText.Infiltrator: Elaru sent you about Martley? Good. Take this cloak; it's the colour of the tents in his camp. Wear it, and his guards may take you for one of their own until it's too late.

TargetText: Martley falls. You wrap his body in the cloak; Adam Glaze will want proof.
Is that Martley? Give him here; there are people who need to see that he's gone.
Adam sent something for me? Hand it over.

FinishText.Infiltrator: Martley's ledger, his letters, and the names of the ones who paid him. Well done, <Player>. Elaru will be pleased, and so am I. Take this.

Description.Infiltrator: <Player>. Your name is starting to be spoken in the right rooms. Now a greater man has asked for us: Sir Bors, who holds the Black Mountains for the King. His man at Snowdonia, Captain Rhodri, needs eyes and ears in places soldiers can't go. That is what we are for. Will you go to [Captain Rhodri]?
Description.Mercenary: <Player>. Word is you don't waste time, which is the best thing anyone can say of a soldier. Sir Bors, who holds the Black Mountains for the King, has asked the Guild for help, and his man at Snowdonia, Captain Rhodri, will tell you the rest. Will you go to [Captain Rhodri]?
Description.Cabalist: <Player>. You have impressed people who are not easily impressed. Sir Bors, who holds the Black Mountains for the King, has asked the Guild for a quiet hand, and his man at Snowdonia, Captain Rhodri, will explain. Will you go to [Captain Rhodri]?
Description.Necromancer: <Player>. Sir Bors, who holds the Black Mountains for the King, has asked for help, and his man at Snowdonia, Captain Rhodri, will explain. You may hear talk of Arawnites. They are not of the Temple: they are zealots who wear our Lord's name and do none of his will. Will you go to [Captain Rhodri]?
Description.Reaver: <Player>. Sir Bors, who holds the Black Mountains for the King, has asked for help, and his man at Snowdonia, Captain Rhodri, will tell you what. You may hear talk of Arawnites. They are not of the Temple: they are zealots who wear our Lord's name and do none of his will. The Temple will not weep for them. Will you go to [Captain Rhodri]?

SourceText: Captain Rhodri keeps the border keep in Snowdonia Fortress, at the north end of the Black Mountains. Go to him.

Before we court them, we must know them. Elrigh drifts from inn to inn in these mountains, and he hears everything; last I heard he was drinking at Snowdonia Station. Find him and ask him about the locals of Barfog.

The Barfog folk are proud, and they hate Camelot, but they'd hate the renegades more if they knew the half of it: a tower full of King's guards who stopped answering to the King, out on the edge of the lake. Andri knows more. He used to serve with them, and now he drinks in the taverns of Camelot.

I served at that tower before it turned. Sir Dillus leads them now; he took the tower and half the garrison with it. They say he takes his orders from someone in the north. I didn't stay to find out who.
StepText: Seek out Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep.
Find Elrigh in the inns of the Black Mountains and ask about the locals of Llyn Barfog. (whisper: locals)
Find Andri in the taverns of Camelot and ask about the renegade guards. (whisper: renegade)
Tell Captain Rhodri of the renegades and Sir Dillus. (whisper: Sir Dillus)
TargetText: So you're the one Camelot sent. Good; I need someone the locals won't know for one of mine. West of here lies Llyn Barfog. Its people keep to themselves and to the old ways, and Sir Bors would have them as friends rather than enemies before this border gets any hotter.
Another traveler with an empty cup. What'll it be, then? Gossip about the [locals] of Barfog? It's always Barfog these days.
Leave me to my drink. Unless... you've come about Barfog? Everyone wants to hear about the [renegade] guards these days.
You're back. What did you learn? Who leads the renegades? Tell me it isn't [Sir Dillus].

FinishText.Infiltrator: Dillus. I served beside him once. If he has turned, this is worse than Sir Bors feared. You have done well, <Player>. Take this, and come back to me when you have earned the title of Spy; there is a renegade in the tower of Llyn Barfog I will need you for.

set.Description: <Player>. We cannot actively move on the renegades without a reason. So we have decided to send you to their tower under the cover of darkness. There you will subdue one of the [renegade guards] and learn all you can.
SourceText: Their tower stands in Llyn Barfog, on your left as you come down from the North Black Mountains. Do not spend much time in the vicinity. The moment you learn of something, return to us. Farewell, <Class>.
Captain Rhodri will want to read it.

'The messenger comes through the pass at the turn of the moon, with word from the north.' The north. Arawnites, if I'm any judge. Find that messenger in the pass to Llyn Barfog and take his orders from him, by whatever means you must.
You can't read a word of it. Omis, the vendor at Swanton Keep, is said to know old scripts.
Arawnite cipher, and an old one. There; I've written what it says between the lines. Take it to your captain, and don't tell anyone who deciphered it for you.
StepText: Slay a renegade guard in Llyn Barfog and learn of their treason.
Bring the guard's diary to Captain Rhodri.
Find the Arawnite messenger in the pass to Llyn Barfog and take his orders.
Have Omis at Swanton Keep decipher the Arawnite orders.
Return the deciphered orders to Captain Rhodri.
TargetText: <Player> notices a book on the guard's belt.
You have something from the tower? Let me see it.
The Arawnite messenger falls. In his satchel are orders, sealed and written in a crabbed, ciphered hand.
Orders, is it? Let me have a look.
Omis could read it? Give it here.

FinishText.Infiltrator: 'Dillus holds the tower. When the border falls, the lake falls with it.' So it's true: Dillus sold the King's tower to the Arawnites. You've given Sir Bors his proof, <Player>. Take this, and come back when you have earned the title of Red Hand.

set.Description: <Player>, it is good to see you are still alive and have come in good health. I have been asked by Sir Bors to ensure this [matter] with the renegades is finished once and for all.
SourceText: Sir Dillus first, and his officers with him. Then go to Twr ap Alsig at the outpost in Llyn Barfog; whatever Dillus carries may be the proof Twr needs.
Twr ap Alsig will want to see this.

Heavens. This is Dillus's own hand, and the Arawnites' seal. I scarcely believe my eyes. Still, a paper is only a paper, and I must be certain where your loyalties lie. The undead cythraul roam this land. Destroy one and bring me its skull, and Barfog will give you the support you seek.
Bring the skull to Twr ap Alsig.
StepText: Slay Sir Dillus and his renegade officers.
Speak to Twr ap Alsig at the outpost in Llyn Barfog, and give him the Arawnite orders as proof of Sir Dillus' betrayal.
Slay a cythraul in Llyn Barfog and bring its skull as proof.
Give Twr ap Alsig the cythraul skull.
TargetText: Sir Dillus falls. Sealed inside his gauntlet is his own copy of the Arawnite orders, signed in his hand.

Yes, <Race>? What do you want? Support, from us? Your kind forgot the old ways long ago; the light of that Camelot has blinded you. We know you killed Dillus, and it has not won you a friend here. If you have proof of anything, give it to me now, before my people lose their patience.
The cythraul crumbles. Its skull rolls free, still cold.
I still seek proof of your deeds. Do you have something for me?
set.FinishText: You have done well, <Race>. Barfog will support your cause and welcome you always. Take this, as a token of trust between our people.

set.Description: Ah, <Player>! You have returned, and just in time as well. We have prepared our case and are ready to leave for Camelot. We wish you to journey to Camelot and inform our Scribe Veral of our wish to lend support to Barfog. Take this as proof of our [intentions]. We will be along shortly.
SourceText: Scribe Veral keeps a house behind Castle Camelot. Put the document into no one's hands but his.
You are from Sir Bors? How can it be you have not seen the [local report] yet?
He was never after Sir Bors. He was waiting for you. Captain Rhodri will want to know.
StepText: Take the document to Scribe Veral, in a house behind Castle Camelot.
Return to the Snowdonia border keep, search it for the assassin (the south-west landing) and slay him.
Speak to Captain Rhodri.
TargetText: Hail traveler! How may I be of service to you?
The assassin gasps as he falls: "I thank thee for the help into the darkness of death. My endurance of life has been paid in full! Peace beckons!"

FinishText.Infiltrator: <Player>! You have done us the greatest of services! These Arawnites have caused us nothing but trouble since you dispatched Sir Dillus. Sir Bors can offer nothing that would fully repay the debt you have fashioned this day. Let this reward be the start of what little we have to offer. In time we shall find greater reward for your deeds, and when that time comes, we shall once again call upon the Guild of Shadows and their most cunning <Class>!

set.Description: <Player>. I have a task for you, should you be [interested].
SourceText: Go to Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep. Listen to everything he says, and to what he doesn't.

Here is a note for him. Kuebler commands the watch at Castle Sauvage; you'll find him upstairs. He won't like being asked questions by anyone outside his chain of command, so let the note do the asking.
Rhodri's lackey, sent all this way to ask whether anything is amiss at Sauvage. Nothing is amiss. Go back to Snowdonia and tell him so.
Then we go around him. Sir Bors has sent a gift for Twr ap Alsig of Barfog: this chest, filled with riches. Give it to him, and speak to him of the goblin uprising.
A generous gift; Sir Bors learns. You wish to speak of the [goblin] uprising?
The dispatch speaks of an attack on the folk of Llyn Barfog. Twr ap Alsig must be warned.
An attack on Barfog! Then it is true. Tell your captain that Barfog asks his help to stop this invasion of dwarves from Midgard. We will not be caught sleeping.

SourceText.Infiltrator: You have done well and Sir Bors would see that you are rewarded. What reward do you desire? [Crackling Impaler], [Death's Touch], [Death Dancer], or [Spark of Midnight]?
SourceText.Mercenary: You have done well and Sir Bors would see that you are rewarded. What reward do you desire? [Crackling Impaler], [Death's Touch], [Glitter], [Spark], [Dazzle], or [Arcing Bludgeoner]?
SourceText.Cabalist: You have done well and Sir Bors would see that you are rewarded. What reward do you desire? [Staff of Eternal Lifeforce], [Staff of Earth Channeling], or [Staff of Spirit Consumption]?

StepText: Seek out Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep. (whisper: speak with Lieutenant Kuebler)
Deliver Rhodri's note to Lieutenant Kuebler in Castle Sauvage.
Return to Captain Rhodri.
Speak to Twr ap Alsig of Barfog about the goblin uprising, and deliver to him Sir Bors' chest.
Seek out a Savant within Tepok's Mine and learn what you can of the passageways. You may be forced to slay the goblin and search his belongings.
Carry the dispatch to Twr ap Alsig within Barfog to warn him of the impending attack.
Return to Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep.

StepText.Infiltrator: Choose your reward: whisper Captain Rhodri the name of the item you want (Crackling Impaler, Death's Touch, Death Dancer, Spark of Midnight).
StepText.Mercenary: Choose your reward: whisper Captain Rhodri the name of the item you want (Crackling Impaler, Death's Touch, Glitter, Spark, Dazzle, Arcing Bludgeoner).

TargetText: Good, you came. Let us get [down to business].
What do you want? A note from Rhodri? Give it here, then.
Back from Sauvage already? And Kuebler sent you away with nothing. Of course he did.
<Race>. Again. What is it you carry this time?
The Savant shrieks as he falls: "My pets shall put you in your place!" Among his belongings is a dwarven dispatch.
You return in haste. What have you found?
This is a great day, <Player>! I shall travel to meet with Twr ap Alsig and his people. Perhaps between us we can once and forever be united as one realm. Well, we can at least hope.

TargetText.Infiltrator: Have you decided? [Crackling Impaler], [Death's Touch], [Death Dancer], or [Spark of Midnight]?
TargetText.Mercenary: Have you decided? [Crackling Impaler], [Death's Touch], [Glitter], [Spark], [Dazzle], or [Arcing Bludgeoner]?

set.FinishText: A fine choice. Carry it well, <Player>; Sir Bors will not forget what you have done for this border.

set.Description: Hail! I trust you are well? I have a mission for you, should you be [interested].
SourceText: Then go to Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep. He is expecting you, though perhaps not so soon.

Good. Twr ap Alsig believes the dwarves have been sending Tepok's goblins money and supplies. I doubt dwarves could stomach such company, but we cannot ignore our newest allies, and that mine has been a thorn for too long. Sir Bors wants you to go down into Tepok's Mine and slay Overseer Tepok himself. He carries a sack of his most precious things; bring it back, for it may tell us who has been helping him.
Captain Rhodri will want to see what is inside.

This is what we've been looking for! Twr ap Alsig has been deceived; I knew the dwarves had nothing to do with this. This letter speaks of supplies from the Pennine Mountains, sent by a people who make their home there. Take this dispatch to Twr ap Alsig so he knows where to look. We would be wise to turn our eyes north.
From Pennine? Not the dwarves at all... I was wrong, and I do not say that often. Tell your captain that Barfog will watch the north.

Very well! While you were away, Sir Bors had his scouts search the borderlands. The goblins had tunnelled under the pass wall to bring in supplies from the north, but our scouts were spotted before they could follow, and the tunnel was destroyed. So we go to the source. Begin with the Tylwyth Teg: their courier Delfina carries reports to and from their homelands. Find her in the Pennine Mountains, slay her, and bring me her reports. Our time is short; do not toy with her guards.
You cannot read them, but Twr ap Alsig might.
There. I have written it plain beneath their script. Take it to your captain; it is his business, not mine.
StepText: Seek out Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep. (whisper: assist us)
Descend into Tepok's Mine, slay Overseer Tepok and take his sack.
Bring Tepok's sack to Captain Rhodri.
Deliver the dispatch to Twr ap Alsig in Llyn Barfog.
Tell Captain Rhodri your work is done. (whisper: work is done)
Infiltrate the Tylwyth Teg camp in the Pennine Mountains and slay the courier Delfina.
Have Twr ap Alsig translate Delfina's reports.
Return the translated reports to Captain Rhodri.
TargetText: I had not expected you so soon; give me a moment to gather my thoughts. It is good to see you in such health. Sir Bors will be pleased it was you who answered his call. We need your skill, and what you know of the folk of Barfog, and you will be well rewarded. Are you still willing to [assist us]?
Overseer Tepok falls. Clutched in his claws is a heavy leather sack.
Ah! Were you able to retrieve Tepok's precious sack? Give it here.
<Race>. Rhodri sends you again. What is it now?
Back again! Did Twr ap Alsig take the dispatch? Then tell me your [work is done], and we can move on.
Delfina falls. Her satchel holds a bundle of reports in the Tylwyth Teg script.
You bring me elvish writing? Give it here; I will read it for you.
Once again your swiftness is impressive! Do you have Delfina's reports?
set.FinishText: This does not bode well. I see no mention of goblins here; our scribes will have to go over them more closely. You have done well, <Class>! We will need you again once we understand what Delfina was carrying. Return to your master in Camelot, and wait for word.

Description.Infiltrator: <Player>. Captain Rhodri has sent for you again, by name. Delfina's reports are read, and whoever is behind the goblin uprising has not been found. Someone is lying to all of us. Will you find the source of this [deceit]?
Description.Mercenary: <Player>. Rhodri's sent for you again, by name this time. Someone's been feeding the goblins, and he still doesn't know who. Somebody's lying to the lot of us. Will you find the source of this [deceit]?
Description.Cabalist: <Player>. Captain Rhodri has asked for you by name. The hand behind the goblin uprising is still hidden, and every trail so far has led nowhere. Will you find the source of this [deceit]?
Description.Necromancer: <Player>. Rhodri asks for you by name. Whoever moves the goblins is still hidden, and the shadows I consult are uneasy. Will you find the source of this [deceit]?
Description.Reaver: <Player>. Rhodri wants you, by name. Whoever's behind the goblins is still hiding, and the Temple wants that someone found. Will you find the source of this [deceit]?

SourceText: Go to Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep.
Their courier travels the Pennine Mountains. Slay him and bring me his documents. And remember: if you are killed or captured, we have no part in it, and we never knew your name.
Captain Rhodri will want these.

These speak of the Ravenclan giants and their Book of Lore. That book holds all they know of their allies and their doings, but my scouts could not learn who carries it. With that book and these documents we may piece together who is behind the goblin uprising. Lieutenant Kuebler at Castle Sauvage knows the Ravenclan; ask him about the book of lore.
Belgrik carries it, the Ravenclan's chief, on his peak in the Pennine Mountains. If you want the book, you'll have to take it from him, and I wish you luck.
Captain Rhodri must see this.

SourceText.Infiltrator: With this book and the isolationist documents we can begin to piece it together. You have earned your reward, <Player>, and I have had it crated and sent to Master Edric in Camelot. Go and see him.
SourceText.Mercenary: With this book and the isolationist documents we can begin to piece it together. You have earned your reward, <Player>, and I have had it crated and sent to Master Arenis in Camelot. Go and see him.
SourceText.Cabalist: With this book and the isolationist documents we can begin to piece it together. You have earned your reward, <Player>, and I have had it crated and sent to Magus Isen in Camelot. Go and see him.
SourceText.Necromancer: With this book and the isolationist documents we can begin to piece it together. You have earned your reward, <Player>, and I have had it crated and sent to Yulia in Camelot. Go and see her.
SourceText.Reaver: With this book and the isolationist documents we can begin to piece it together. You have earned your reward, <Player>, and I have had it crated and sent to Peze in Camelot. Go and see him.

StepText: Seek out Captain Rhodri at the Snowdonia border keep.
Slay the isolationist courier in the Pennine Mountains and take his documents.
Return the documents to Captain Rhodri.
Speak with Lieutenant Kuebler at Castle Sauvage about the Ravenclan giants' Book of Lore.
Slay the Ravenclan giant Belgrik in the Pennine Mountains and take the Book of Lore.
Return the Book of Lore to Captain Rhodri.

StepText.Infiltrator: Report to Master Edric in Camelot.
StepText.Mercenary: Report to Master Arenis in Camelot.
StepText.Cabalist: Report to Magus Isen in Camelot.

TargetText: <Player>. It took time to decipher Delfina's reports and be sure they were no fake; many scouts lost their lives proving them. They are genuine, but of little use. Sir Bors and I agree we must turn from the Tylwyth Teg to the isolationists of the Pennine Mountains. They pose no threat, I think; they only wish to be left alone. But they may hold vital information, and we must be thorough and not let our feelings cloud us.
The isolationist courier falls. His documents are wrapped in oilcloth, as if they were worth more than he was.
You have the courier's documents? Let me see.
You again. Rhodri's lackey. What is it now? The Ravenclan's book of lore? ...Fine.
Belgrik falls with a sound like a landslide. Beneath him lies a great iron-bound Book of Lore.
Is that the Ravenclan's Book of Lore? Give it here, carefully.

FinishText.Infiltrator: <Player>, I am very proud of you, and so is Captain Rhodri; he holds you in high esteem. It is a very good thing to have someone so close to Sir Bors think so highly of you. This crate came for you from Snowdonia, with a note in his hand.
FinishText.Mercenary: <Player>. Proud of you, and Rhodri thinks the world of you; that's worth more than coin, with him so close to Sir Bors. This crate came from Snowdonia for you. There's a note with it.
FinishText.Cabalist: <Player>, I am very proud of you, and Captain Rhodri holds you in high esteem; it is no small thing to be thought so well of by someone so close to Sir Bors. This crate came for you from Snowdonia, with a note in his hand.
FinishText.Necromancer: <Player>, I am proud of you, and so is Captain Rhodri; he holds you in high esteem, and he stands close to Sir Bors. Arawn sees all debts. This crate came for you from Snowdonia, with a note in his hand.
FinishText.Reaver: <Player>. Proud of you, and Rhodri thinks highly of you; he stands close to Sir Bors, and that counts. This crate came from Snowdonia for you, with a note from him.

Description.Infiltrator: <Player>. The Ellyll grow ever more involved in all this, and Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage wants someone to learn more of them and of their defences. I told him I would send you. Will you go to [Sir Tilian]?
Description.Mercenary: <Player>. The Ellyll are mixed up in this deeper every day, and Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage wants someone to get a look at their defences. That's you. Will you go to [Sir Tilian]?
Description.Cabalist: <Player>. The Ellyll grow ever more involved, and Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage seeks someone to learn more of them and of their defences. Will you go to [Sir Tilian]?
Description.Necromancer: <Player>. The Ellyll grow bolder, and the dead whisper of them. Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage seeks someone to learn more of them and of their defences. Will you go to [Sir Tilian]?
Description.Reaver: <Player>. The Ellyll are in this deeper every day. Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage wants someone to learn their defences. Will you go to [Sir Tilian]?

SourceText: Sir Tilian waits at Castle Sauvage, at the top of the keep. Hear him out.
Travel to the Ellyll village in the Pennine Mountains and slay one of their seers. They keep journals; bring the journal to Captain Rhodri in Snowdonia Fortress.
Captain Rhodri must see this journal.
StepText: Talk to Sir Tilian at Castle Sauvage.
Slay an Ellyll seer in the villages of the Pennine Mountains and take his journal.
Give the journal to Captain Rhodri, upstairs in Snowdonia Fortress.
TargetText: So you are the one who found the Book of Lore. Good. The Ellyll are deeper in this than any of us thought, and their seers write down everything.
The Ellyll seer falls. His journal is full of bargains, and one name appears on every page.
Sir Tilian sent you? Do you have the seer's journal?

FinishText.Infiltrator: Lord Elidyn. The same name, on every page. Sir Tilian was right. Come back to me when you have earned the title of Master Infiltrator, <Player>.
FinishText.Mercenary: Lord Elidyn. The same name, on every page. Sir Tilian was right. Come back to me when you have earned the title of Mercenary Master, <Player>.
FinishText.Cabalist: Lord Elidyn. The same name, on every page. Sir Tilian was right. Come back to me when you have earned the title of Cleric Prime, <Player>.
FinishText.Necromancer: Lord Elidyn. The same name, on every page. Sir Tilian was right. Come back to me when you have earned the title of Master Reanimator, <Player>.
FinishText.Reaver: Lord Elidyn. The same name, on every page. Sir Tilian was right. Come back to me when you have earned the title of Dark Knight, <Player>.

SourceText: Elidyn holds the old Ellyll ruins on the hill in the Pennine Mountains, and he will not be alone. Take friends, go carefully, and come back to me.
Captain Rhodri is waiting at the Snowdonia border keep.
TargetText: Lord Elidyn falls, and with him every lie he spun across the border.

FinishText.Infiltrator: Lord Elidyn is dead, and his lies with him. Sir Bors will hear of this before nightfall. Take this armour, <Class>; the Guild of Shadows makes it only for its finest.
FinishText.Mercenary: Lord Elidyn is dead, and his lies with him. Sir Bors will hear of this before nightfall. Take this armour, <Class>; the Guild of Shadows makes it only for its finest.

TargetText: Ah. G'day. And who might you be? I see, you're a <Class>. Has Mistress Laws, Master Reginald, or Delore sent you here to help me out? Why don't they just send you out after the goo? That's all I really want. You know, I don't remember that there were that many of these strange creatures crawling around the village [before]. Yes, well, before, well, before they came. Don't you remember? That night? All day long, everything's fine. Set itself uop for a fine next day, as well! The night, it was clear. Not a sign of a storm in sight! Why, no one prepared for it! Then, in the darkest part, suddenly, the storm starts! We were woken from the noise of it! It was awful, but we didn't dare go outside! Some of the men, they did, but they came back pale as a corpse! Were shaken to their core! And some of these being the fightin' men! Best of the town! Aye, but the [swamp goo]. They've gotten into the food cellar! The slimy things were creeping all over that place! I've gotten rid of most of the swamp goo, but I know there's more just outside town working their way to my food stores. I think you could do a small favor for us all and get rid of some. Oh and while you are at it, the skin of the swamp goo, I've some uses for it. I'll pay you for a swamp goo skin. Just go and get me one of their skins, and I'll be satisfied with ya. Oh, you're back! Did you see how many there were? They are a nuisance, aren't they! Well, have you got me the skin? Ah, a good and slimy one! It's odd, these creatures, they've got some strangeness about them, but they've got their uses, as well. Thank you, then. Here, I promised I'd pay ya, and I will!

Greetings young <Class>. What be thy name? Well, <Player>, I see that Magess Gwenllian has been doing her part to help improve the relations around her. You may not have noticed, but many people around here do not like Inconnu. I am not one of those people, but there is a man, a poison merchant just came to this land, Burton MacDougal, who believes that every last Inconnu us out to steal his soul. I have told him that I can [prove differently]. I told Burton that the Inconnu brought a poison with them that is very effective against Drakoran. He said he would believe that there Inconnu are here to help if he could get a sample of the poison and the list of components to make it himself. Lirele, an Inconnu who is working with us, has agreed to help but she needs [a certain component] to finish the poison. Lirele told me she needed the fin (of) a sea pup to complete the poison. They live in the waters around Gothwaite Harbor. Get one and take it to Lirele. [Step #2] Get the fin of a sea pup from the waters outside Gothwaite Harbor. Sea pups are located just to the end of town near the water's edge. Get a fin and take it to Lirele.
Thank you. This should only take a minute. Here, take the poison and this scroll to Burton MacDougal. Tell him it is from Lirele the Inconnu.

What do you want? I don't like your kind, so state your business quickly and get gone! Oh, you're from Lirele, eh? That doesn't change anything. That nasty Trynt told me the pale witch would be getting me some poison, but I haven't seen it yet. Did she send you over here with it? Let me have it. Hrmph, haven't seen something like this before. but this won't last me very long. Trynt said she'd tell me how to make it. I see the wench hasn't lived up to that promise. You just can't trust you Inconnu! Oh, hrmph, well, um, this is how to make it. Um, well, I guess that wench, er, Lirele, wasn't lying to me after all. Maybe she's not so bad after all, or you either, but I still don't trust the rest of 'em! Well, here, since you did some work, you can have this. But t his doesn't mean that I like you! Now, buy some poison or get out of here!

set.Description: Remember the swamp goo in the cellar? And the sickness that affected the Inconnu only? It seems that there is an undead that has been hiding from Arawn for years, Now, with the Inconnu walking the land, he's feeling [threatened].

set.FinishText: This was Thulin's most prized possession. He gave it to me before he left on his fatal trip, telling me it was time to pass it on to another. I know I can not put it to use, perhaps you can. Here is al littler coin as well. I know it isn't much, but perhaps it will aid you in your battles. Thank you again friend. Even though these are sad times, I am strenghtened by your courage and kind heartedness. Thank you.
SourceText: Oh! You will! Excellent! Thank you so much! I am very worried for my Thulin's safety, and I would hope you find him alive, but if you don't, please bring his [remains] back to me.

TargetText: Well hello young one. What is your [name]? Well, it is a pleasure to meet you. I enjoy meeting all the young Vikings throughoout our [realm]. Did you know that the [art] of trapping is very important here in Midgard, for everyone? Yes, [trapping] is an art, the skinning of an animal, preserving the pelt and tanning it for use. Trapping and doing these things correctly can [fetch] you a good deal of popularity to traders and bring in a nice profit. Go in to woods and see if yo ucan capture fice tawny lynx cubs and bring their pelts to me so that I may prepare them. You have done a wonderful [job] and these pelts will work quite nicely. I shall begin preserving and tanning these skins shortly. Once they are finished tanning I may have another job for you.

set.Description: Hail. I am Torold, and I shall be your trainer in this wild land. King Goran Stonefist and his brother Stonelock have charged me with training all young Vikings to prepare them to join the ranks of King Goran's army to aid in the exploration of Aegir. Aegir is a wild, untamed place, and it's made even more dangerous for a your <Class> like you by the presence of [Morvaltar].
TargetText: Lo, I see a young <Class> before me. What is your name? Speak up! You are here to prove that you have the strength in you to endure in this land. The trial is simple in nature, but unless you are strong, may prove difficult to execute. You must venture out and face [one of the creatures] that roam this land. You must seek out a marine fungus. They may be found in the waters south and southwest of here. Find one and defeat it. Once you have, obtain proof that you have accomplished this test. Return to me here. So, you managed to survive, but anyone can run away. Show me the proof you defeated the marine fungus. Well done. I do not like to be so rough with young Vikings, but I must be. I do not want to see anyone die because I failed to do my job. But you have proven that you have the potential for great strength. I shall let your trainer know of your success.

<Class>, here to do some [exploring]? Aye, I could use your aid, if you don't mind a bit of danger. You see, there's some minerals embedded in some rocks not too far from here. Now it's not a whole mine or anything, but I want to know what sort of mineral it is. There's one [problem]. Aye, there's some creatures about that make it hard to get to. Now, I'd go and fight off the creatures myself, but you know, I've got some work to do here, and really can't be bothered. That's why I'm [willing to pay] you. Ha! Of course I'm going to pay! I've been here long enough to know nobody's here for the pleasure of being here! Everyone wants something! Land! Treasure! Fame! Whatever it is. Well, are you [satisfied] I'll pay you? There are some stray scimitar cubs near the mineral deposit. Remove the cubs to find the deposit. Many cuvs are found bsouthwest, just past the bridge. Ah, then did you find the thing I was looking for? Any of those rocks with those mineral bits on 'em? Great! I'm sure we can sort out what this is, and where we might find some more, if it proves to be any use! I've got a whole bunch of dwarven clans just eeking for a reason to come out here! If I can sell them on this area, I'll get a nice fee! Ah, but I promised you a fee as well, didn't I? Well then, I'll keep my word friend. Here you are! Good working with your <Class>.

SourceText: Ah a brave <Class> you are! Great! Go speak to Nibalk. He will tell you more.

set.FinishText: Ah! I must tell you, Longbeard and Ota have been crawling all over each other and everyone else in the town to get this beast! They both want to claim it as their prize! Ha! Well, not that I want to get involved in the in-fighting on the dwarven kobold expedition, but really, somebody had to end this Ibicus obsession once and for all. I figured it'd be a better thing for me to have Ibicus. That way, Longbeard and Ota can't spend precious time trying to outdo each other. Oh! But imagine the looks they will have when they see Ibicus! Just a small benefit from all this! Here, I promised you a reward, though. Thanks. You've be a great help!
SourceText: It's known as Ibicus. When you kill it, bring me it's carcass, and you will be well rewarded.

TargetText: Greetings <Class>. I see that your trainer received the message fromt he Defenders. What is your name? We have quite a task ahead of us. I was once a Scout for the Defenders of Albion before I hurt my leg. Since I can no longer do my duty, the Defenders have helped set me up s as merchant. It's not what I had planned to be doing , but it puts food on my table. Even though I am not an active member of the Defenders, I still do what I can to help. Lately that has meant [tracking down lost objects]. As you may know, the Defenders of Albion are always searching for better ways to defend the realm from enemies. Our duty is hard, for these days we face not onlythe enemies that nip at our borders but also the ones that exist amongst us. Anything that can be done or used to make our fight a little easier is always well supported among the Defenders. That is [why I was sent] here. One of the Inconnu that has been helping us to defend the realm against the Drakoran located and recovered a stone that seems to weaken the Drakoran. Our Theurgists back in Camelot wish to examine and study this stone so that it can possibly be duplicated and used to aid us in this fight. If we [only had it now]! This Inconnu was coming back from getting the stone when he was attacked and overpowered by a pack of urchin rabblerousers. They stole the stone and ran off into the wilds when the Inconnu mandaged to crawl back here. So far no one has been able to capture the little rabblerouser that has it. Go now and seek out the urchin rabblerouser that has it. They are tricky and throw it around, so keep trying until you find it. We are counting on you. Were you able to find the stone? The Defenders in Albion are waiting for it so they can begin trying to duplicate it. I must send it to them soon. This isn't the stone I seek! I was told it was plain, flat, gray stone. It may have special properties, but the Defenders will have to investigate it. Did you find another stone? This stone doesn't look like it will do much, but we hope that it will. I shall get this over to Camelot right away. The Defenders of Albion sent this over for the person who was able to recover the lost stone. Here take it, and know that you have helped to defend the realm!

set.FinishText: Here you are friend. I had my compatriot, Averrius, look over the silk. He said it had properties that would benefit someone like you. I hope you can use it for some time to come. Again, I think you for all your hard work!

TargetText: Hail and well met! You look like a <Class> with a purpose for coming here. I don't think you seek a shield, but perhaps [information]? I thought so! I figured Thorgil would have to send someone in his place, since I've heard others say that Inga has begun teaching him the art of making and selling arrows. I was very sorry to hear that Thorgil has lost his farm to the tomtes. I was so busy selling shields that I hadn't had a chance to get over and speak with him about what happened. I was glad when he came in here the other day [to ask me] about the tomtes. I don't know much, but as Thorgil probably told you, my cousins do. When Thorgil came to me, I couldn't say no to his plea for help. I went and visited each of my brothers and told them of Thorgil's situation. They were both very intrigued by the whole thing, for they have been watching the tomtes around here for many years. Both said they recently observed some changes in [the tomtes' behaviour]. They both spent a few days watching the tomtes and then trying to make sense of what they saw. I recently received word from both of them, telling me who Thorgil should speak to. But since you are helping Thorgil, I shall tell you [which of my cousins] to speak to. Both sent me word that they think Edvard would be the best one to help Thorgil. He has noticed some happenings around the tomte camps he watches that his brother Emmerick hasn't noticed. Most people don't know where Edvard likes to hide so I shall tell you. Go across the stone bridge northeast of here to the guard tower. You will find him on the top most level. Take care in climbong the ladders, they can be tricky! Remember to tell him Thorgil sent you!

Yes? Is there something I can do for you? I am rather busy, and I am also waiting for someone. Oh he did? Well then, you are the one I am waiting for. My cousin Hulda said that Thorgil was having problems with the tomtes. I wasn't surprised to hear it, because I have been watching them and I have noticed a change in their behavior lately. Most of the time they just pester people traveling along the road or thos that stray too close to the camps. But as I watched, I noticed that the tomtes were organizing [specific attacks]. I believe that the tomtes are trying to find a way to push the people of Audliten and its surrounding area off the lands that once belonged to the tomtes. As more people have moved into the area, the tomtes have been pushed to smaller and smaller areas. There are only a few camps left around here, and because of that ,the residents around here have grown to think the tomtes have moved on or disappeard from this world. But that is [far from the truth]! The tomtes needed a place that wouldn't be taken over by the residents of the area. They searched and found a cave not far from where my brother watches them. They are crafty little men, and began to carve out a home for themselves under the earth. They worked quickly, and soon their new home was ready. Led by the strongest of the tomtes, Nisse, most of them left their lands and headed deep underground. Now, some people believe that the tomtes in the camps around here don't like dank surroundings of the cave, but that isn ot true. There is [another reason] they live above ground. All this time the tomtes have been planning ways to remove the inhabitants of Audliten and the surrounding areas and reclaim them for their own. The tomtes that live in the camps above ground are the eyes and ears for Nisse and report back everything they see. Recently I've noticed more messengers heading down from the north, yet my brother has not noticed and unusual activity around the entrance to the tomte caves. That has led us both to believe [someone else] is behind this plot to drive Thorgil and the others from this area off their land. I've noticed many messengers heading in and out of the camp of Edigo. It's my guess that something is going on and he knows about it. I've watched Edigo for some time now and I know he is plotting something. Most likely he's kept the messages that have been sent to him. You must get those messages so we can figure out what is going on and who is sending them. Edigo's camp is not far off from here. Head back through Audliten and take the road east out of town. Go over the stone bridge and keep going until you see the wooden tower. It's not far from Thorgil's old house. You will find Edigo there, but do not go alone! The other tomtes will anwer Edigo's call for help. Return to me when you have any messages. [Step #4] Slay Edigo and obtain any tomte messages. Go through Audliten and head east out of town. Cross the stone bridge and continue to the wooden tower near Thorgil's farm house. (Note: Another possible path for step 4: "Slay Ocug to obtain the tomte messages. To find him, swim across the river beside the guard tower, then head east up the coast to the tomte camp. Do not face Ocug alone! I am impressed. I watched over your battle with the tomtes from here and I liked what I saw. Thorgil did well in selecting you to help him. Now, let's see the messages you obtained. It's good you brought these to me. They happen to be written in the ancient language of the tomtes, and my brother and I are experts at reading and writing it. It seems that Edigo has been following orders to drive the inhabitants of Audliten and the surrounding areas away and reclaim the land. I'm not surprised to see that the orders were issued by Smack. He has always been [eager to succeed]. A long time ago, Smack displeased Nisse and was forced to leave the tomte caves and live among the races of Midgard. Since then, he has been working to get back into Nisse's good graces. It seems that he thinks if he can clear the land of invaders, as he sees them, then Nisse will be pleased and restore him to the position he once held. It appears that SMack has recruited Edigo to help in his plot. But now that Edigo is dead, Smack will try to recruit another of the tomtes. You must [stop Smack]! Gather your forces and lead t hem to Smack's stronghold. You must stop him from contacting any of the other camp leaders. Smack's stronghold isn't hard to find. Take the road east out of Audliten again, and cross the stone bridge. Continue down the road until you see a small stone fort to the southeast. That is where you will find Smack. While you are off dealing with Smack, I shall send word to Thorgil of what you are doing. Return to him when you are finished with Smack.

You were? That's wonderful! You have solved one of the problems I was dealing with. I did not know how I was going to get his belongings to him. I heard about his adventure with the horse and do not wish to repeat it. I am not skilled at riding, and I fear I would break something too. But if you are here to collect his things, then I will not have to ride a horse. Now, if only I [had his belongings] to give to you! There was a disagreement between the rwo werewolves, and the one left, taking some of the others with him. They came here to Myrkwood and settled into the forest, not far from here. At first, the residents if the town, Askheim, did not know of their presence. Understand that back then, the werewolves had a human form during the day. It has only been over time that they changed and assumed the form the have today. I do not know the entire story, but I know that something bad happened and it resulted in the werewolves taking over [Askheim]. The werewolves that live there now raise their young and let them tear up the land and terrorize the people. It was those pups that attacked me and stole Trustan's favorite sword. I know Trustan would want it back, and I'd go and get it from him, but have some other things of his to find. Trustan loaned a few of this things to another friend and I must get those things back before I can send everything up to him. Please, seek out the werewolf pups that scamper behind Gna Faste and get back Trustan's sword. Please! It is good to see you back. Please give me Trustan's sword so I can make sure it is undamaged. Good, the sword was not damaged by those little fiends. Trustan will be happy, but he would be happier if I was able to return all his things. I received a note from Curka in Galplen. She's the one that Trustan loaned his shield to before he went to Huginfell. I need to get that shield back, but apparently Curka ran into some trouble with [the arachites] on her way here. The arachites are another group that like to cause trouble around here, but Curka can tell you more about them. Here, take this and grab a horse to Galplen. It's not far, but it can be dangerous getting there. Seek out Curka and tell her Atzar sent you for the shield. Once you have it come back to me, and then we'll send you up to Trustan! I see you have recovered the shield from Curka. Excellent. Hold on to it for now. I am almost ready to send Trustan's things to him, but there is one more thing [to recover]. I'm sure Curka talked about the svartlafs when you were with her. She always talks about them and how bad they get treated. Well, I can see why they get treated that way after what they did to me! While you were away, I wanted to get a peek at what the werewolves were up to. Living so close to Askheim, it's natural to want to know what's going on. While I was out in the forest I got attacked by the svartalfs! They seemed to think I [support the werewolves]. I know where these svartalfs who attacked me like to hide. Take the road south from here until you get to the rock that directs you to Galplen. Then you need to go east into the woods. They hide way back in the woods, so be careful! Just south of there you will find a full camp of the svartalfs! If they don't like you, and they may not after you get that helm back, they will attack. Oh, before you go, give me that shield so I can pack it up. Excellent! Now, hurry to find those svartalfs and get the helm back. I see you carry Trustan's helm. This is excellent. I have the rest of his things bundled up. Here, take them and a ticket to Huginfell and go take this stuff to him!

Hello there. Would you like to purchase something or is there something else I can do for you? The shield? What shield? OH! You mean Trustan's shield. You must have been sent by Atzar. That shield is going to [be a problem]. I don't have the shield, the arachites do. Atzar must have mentioned the arachites. They are these spidery type people that live in Myrkwood. Worst thing that ever happened to Myrkwood were those arachites. They didn't start off the way they are, you know. A very long time ago they were spiders. But Myrkwood is a dark forest, and sometimes strange things happen. The power of Myrkwood [affected those spiders]. I had taken Trustan's shield over to Nalliten to show it to a friend of mine who wants to make his own shield. I went there and spent a few days helping my friend make his shield. It was on my way back that I ran into trouble. A group of arachite younglings ran out of the forest and attacked me. They screamed at me, saying those that helped the svartalfs would die. Apparently they could sense my friendship with them. I had to run or else I would have been killed. I threw Trustan's shield at them and ran for the guard tower. They picked up the shield and ran the other way. Now I fear the shield is [lost forever] You know, you look strong enough to handle those arachite younglings. I am not brave or strong, which is why I ran for the guards at the first sight of trouble. Please, go find these younglings and kill them for me. It is the only way to retrieve Trustan's shield, and it will set you on the raod towards building a good relationship with the svartalfs. Head out through the northeast gate and follow the road. When you reach a split in the road, keep going straight to the guard tower. At the tower, head southwest into the woods. You will find the younglings there. Return to me when you have the shield. Good job! I can see that you have Trustan's shield in your pack. It's hard to hide a shield, is it not? You do not appear to have to other things that Trustan left with Atzar, so I think I better send you back to [Atzar]. Here take this ticket to Gna Faste. The horses are so much faster than walking! I shall send word to Trustan that you retrieved his shield so he can make you a nice present for your work. He's quite the craftsman! Now, hurry along to Gna Faste!

She's the one that Trustan loaned his shield to before he went to Huginfell. I need to get that shield back, but apparently Curka ran into some trouble with [the arachites] on her way here. The arachites are another group that like to cause trouble around here, but Curka can tell you more about them. Here, take this and grab a horse to Galplen. It's not far, but it can be dangerous getting there. Seek out Curka and tell her Atzar sent you for the shield. Once you have it come back to me, and then we'll send you up to Trustan! I see you have recovered the shield from Curka. Excellent. Hold on to it for now. I am almost ready to send Trustan's things to him, but there is one more thing [to recover]. I'm sure Curka talked about the svartlafs when you were with her. She always talks about them and how bad they get treated. Well, I can see why they get treated that way after what they did to me! While you were away, I wanted to get a peek at what the werewolves were up to. Living so close to Askheim, it's natural to want to know what's going on. While I was out in the forest I got attacked by the svartalfs! They seemed to think I [support the werewolves]. I know where these svartalfs who attacked me like to hide. Take the road south from here until you get to the rock that directs you to Galplen. Then you need to go east into the woods. They hide way back in the woods, so be careful! Just south of there you will find a full camp of the svartalfs! If they don't like you, and they may not after you get that helm back, they will attack. Oh, before you go, give me that shield so I can pack it up. Excellent! Now, hurry to find those svartalfs and get the helm back. I see you carry Trustan's helm. This is excellent. I have the rest of his things bundled up. Here, take them and a ticket to Huginfell and go take this stuff to him!
Darrius has truly outdone himself this time. I do now see the oddities of which he spoke about in his last letter. Now friend, there is [more to be done].

You continue to amaze me brave Kayje. Now, before this rite can be performed, you must take this bundle to Averrius, in Myrkwood. He is an enchanter and can open the magic within these pieces so I may properly focus on the corruption.
The package, thank you friend, thank you. Please wait while I perform this rite and cease the corruption of the Blodfelag once and for all.

Interesting, very interesting. Let me see what I can do with this. Please wait. I am finished. You may return these to Yver. He will now be able to do his rite. I hope he discovers who is behind all this.

While I though it was merely a legend, something to scare children with at night, I see now that I have been a fool. There is a spider of immense power called the [Widower] who roams the woods of Myrkwood.

So, Averrius, I should have known. You Arachite traitor! How dare you defile Midgard with your devious magic! We shall destroy you! You have done well young Kayje. I wish to reward you for your valiant attempts. I will make you a shield with the parts from his carapace. Let me imbue them with the power of Valhalla. This will only take a moment. Here you are. Use this shield well, and never forget the lessons we both learned here today.

Within Salisbury there exist eleven druid circles, eight major, three minor, and the axis circle where you obtained the darkenstone. Of the three minor circles, one lay in the south and two in the north. All others can be considered major including Stonehenge itself. If a darkenstone is taken into any of these circles, the holder will be made aware if it is major or minor. Each of the minor circles can be instructed to offer up a ley crystal by using the darkenstone. It will be the ley crystal that will allow you to [ switch ] the wells on. As the last rays of light fade from Salisbury, travel to each major druid ring and make use of your crystal. The crystal will be crushed in the process and will activate the ring's well. As Morgana's power has hold of the tombs below these rings, I am unsure what the mix of necromantic power and ley energy will have upon you and the circle itself. Be prepared for anything! If you find yourself without a ley crystal return to a minor circle and use the darkenstone to gain another. If you are foolish enough to lose your darkenstone, you may return to the [ axis circle ] and kill a skeleton to obtain another. All seven of the wells can only be activated using darkness. If dawn arrives and you have not visited all seven you must wait till the next night to complete the ritual. When you have established the alignment of these ley lines, travel to the heart of Stonehenge and use your darkenstone for the final time. Upon the stone's destruction the bonds that tie the portal close should ignite and allow it to be [ opened from the other side ]. You must be ready for Glasan at this point. When the arch druid arrives, you will have little time to attack him, as his power will grow quickly. If you are successful in slaying him, the staff should shatter on its own. Any shards left from the battle must be returned to me! Here, take these instructions to aid you. Good luck to thee <Class>.

Eh? What do you think you are [looking] at, ugly (your characters race)? What? Are you as stupid as you look? Maybe not, eh. You come down here with big ideas and try to do good deeds. I say the faster you go get yourself killed, the better. Wait a [second]! You are that idiot who killed Malroch. Hehe, that was pretty foolish of you. Everyone in Darkness Falls has heard of you and is looking to cash in on the [bounty] for your head. What? Do you think mortals are the only ones who use bounties? Any demon that slays you is supposed to be rewarded by the Master, but I have seen how he rewards his followers. I used to be one of the strongest demons in the Master's army and now look at me. The Master changed me into an imp as [punishment] for something I had nothing to do with. How was I supposed to know the Master already had a plan? Anyway now I am really upset and I need your help to get some revenge on a few demons. If you help me I will tell you things that may just keep you alive a tad longer in the future. Let's say I know something about an ambassador that has been helping the lands of Albion to an early [demise]. I thought that might get your attention, but before I start telling what I know, I want some proof that you can handle yourself in battle. After all, you might have just been lucky when you beat the poor old Malroch. I want you to sneak into the area where the dragon of your land sleeps and return with something for me. You do this for me and I will tell you something of what I [know]. Let's see. What should I have you get, eh? I know! I want a granite gem from a granite giant stonebreaker living in southwestern [Dartmoor]. They dig up some very interesting gems in those mountains. If you are wondering if you can trust me, don't worry your mind any longer. You can trust me, and I can't trust you. That keeps things simple in our future dealings. Now bring me what I want and stop wasting my time. [Step 3] Journey to southwestern Dartmoor and retrieve Granite Gem from a granite giant stonebreaker. Killed Granite Giant Stonebreaker at Dartmoor loc=11k 43k, got gem. Back to Mystemas in DF. Oh, you are back. I suppose you have what I asked for? Well maybe you are not as weak as I thought, but certainly as smart as I thought. So lets talk shall we? I know a few things that would turn you pale with fear. What do I [know], you ask? Well I am glad that you asked. My Master has sent forth an ambassador to your lands to convince your king that the main threat to Albion from the other realms is far greater than the [threat] darkness falls presents. This was done to increase the casualties on both sides of your stupid war. Each time a mortal falls in combat, we take a small portion of that creature's spirit and create one of the soultorn that roam deeper in Darkness Falls. The soultorn are then trained to fight in my Master's armies. See the brilliance of this [plan]? The more you fight, the more you die. The more you die, the stronger we get. Hehe, very nice eh? Master also has a method to get the freshest and strongest of your [spirits]. He watches which of your three realms is strongest on the field of battle and then allows only that realm to directly enter Darkness Falls. We can make far stronger soultorn from those that die here. In fact, once in a while we get very lucky and trap an entire creature's spirit here. There has been an especially strong [soultorn] captured recently. She was a foolish healer named Caisha who came here looking for her lost friend. Now our Princess is torturing her spirit so we can make it into a succubi. Prince Ba'alorian wants to use her in his army as a high priestess or something. Wait, I have an [idea]. You might be able to help both of us at the same time. The Ambassador normally stays at the Princess's side. You will need proof to take to your king that he is being lied to and the Ambassador should be carrying plans from the Prince that will help convince your king. You can help me by taking [Caisha's spirit]. If the Prince has her for a high priestess, I doubt I will ever get a chance to gain my Master's favor again. I would surely like to see the Prince's plan fail miserably and you would provide me the means to do that. So let me make it clear what you [need to do]. First, slay the ambassador and get his pouch of documents to take back to your king or whatever. Second, slay the Princess and her followers. You mst then slay Caisha's soultorn to release her spirit from its torment. Take this Soulstone. It will capture Caisha's spirit when she is slain so that no other demon captures her. Oh, one other [thing]. If you get captured, I will do everything within my power to ensure the inquisitors shred every last piece of your spirit before you can tell anyone our little plan. Do you [Understand] me? Good. Now get going before someone sees us talking. Bring me Caisha like a good little <Class> Reward: Perfect Life Stone Free account required to post You must log in or create an account to post messages. SourceText: Excellent. I am glad to know you are with me. Here is what we must do. There is a Siabra chief by the name of Nasco. He wanders around Shannon Estuary, and is guarded by his Ambushers and Waylayers. He is sneaky and crafty. You will need all the help you can get. Hurry to Howth and speak with my sister, Keriann. She will be able to assist you further in this endeavor for Hibernia.

set.FinishText: Elizabeth will be most pleased to finally receive this. There is a Berserker going over to Mularn soon and I shall send this with her. I sent word to Elizabeth that a <Class> was helping me and she sent this over in thanks. Please take it, knowing that you have helped to protect Midgard!

set.Description: Hail <Class>! Many great adventures await you, but you must first become aware of our past. [Anrid], a powerful Spiritmaster has decided to lead you along this path. Perhaps with her teaching and your adventurous spirit, the Grenlock clan can once again be united!
SourceText: I am glad to see you follow the path of the House of Hel! Anrid can be found at a tavern near the north gate of this city. Good hourney to you <Class>!
TargetText: Sit down my friend and let me tell you [a tale], a tale that you must understand to someday break the spirit bond in the northland. Many hundreds of years ago there was a great clan of Norsemen in the northland of Midgard. They were known as the Grenlock clan, and of them was a great chieftain who strove for peace and kinship among the people. the great man, chieftain Svan Alfevsin lived and worked among his people and was greatly respected. It seems that [history] is never kind to the good hearted, like Svan Alfevson. A great tragedy befell the northlands and their king. An unnatural winter befell the land of the north, known as Urfenlong, freezing the land and water tributaries solid. Being that the Grenlock clan had always lived in a harsh climate they prepared each year with grains and livestock for a harsh winter. However, nothing could have prepared them for the [Urfenlong]. In the third year of the Urfenlong, the land and the seasons were locked in a frozen icy grip. Svan Alfevson called upon his four sons and told them to begin gathering the northland armies and supplies still left. The old king wished for his sons to move the armies and peoples of the Grenlock southward to safety, away from the impending doom of the ice. Great ice sheets moved like living things in the far north, devouring everything in their path and the farthest points of civilization had already succumbed to [the ice]. As the ice moved closer and closer to Svergren Keep, the old king met with his sons one last time. Svan removed his own armor and divided it among his sons keeping only his helmet. Next the king took the Grenlock Crest, the family seal from upon the Keep's wall and with the blade of his battleaxe broke the seal into five pieces. Once again Svan divided the pieces of the crest, just as he did his own armor, and gave a piece to each of his four sons and [kept a piece] for himself. Svan's intention was that one-day, after the terrible unyielding winter that he and his sons would once again reunite and bring the Grenlock clan back together. Several says after Svan's sons left the northland, Svergird's Keep and its ancient stone walls were swept away by the white tide of ice and snow. The terrible storm took the old king with it, and all which remained of the northland. Svan's four sons, Coplin, Gunnar, Ove, and Div marched southward, tearing through [unknown territory]. They passed through Odin's Gate and into the untamed lands continuing to push southward, where they hoped the storm could not reach. The brothers hoped that the mountains of Odin's Gate would hold back the sheets of traveling ice, yet they knew it was not safe to stay that far north. The people of the northland continued to push forward for two years, never settling, always living in fear of what could come over the mountains and sweep them away. A year later due to starvation and exhaustion, the brothers stopped the clan and settled near the sea, [nestled safely] in the mountains near what is now Vasudheim. They hoped that the mountains would stop any invading force, including the elements. It just so happens that the brothers settled in the area that is known today as Jordheim. After several more years the clan had settled in their new home. The brothers once again gathered armies from the north. The intention was for the four of them to split up in the four directions, north, east, south, and west, and explore the new territory they would call home. [Siv was the first] of the brothers to push out of their new home and travel westward. Siv, the youngest of the brothers, put together a small following of an army and led them westward to that shore. Siv and his men settled in the area that is now known as East Svealand. It was here that his followers settled a small township and continued to explore the area in which they perceived to call home. Siv continued to live in East Svealand to the [end of his days] in peace. It is rumored that his [spirit still walks] the lands which he inhabited. You would be wise to seek Siv out and prove this rumor true! Hail! Are you [ready to continue] along the path to unification? As you know Siv had three more brothers. The second brother Coplin decided since Siv was making new settlements outside of their new home that he would patrol the land. Coplin's goal was to protect all those who survived the journey from the northland. Coplin made friends with many of the creatures that lived in the surrounding areas. It was his goal to make pacts with these creatures so that the land would stay [safe] for all those that lived there, both human and creature. Coplin was very successful in this attempt and many aggressions were worked through. Therefore many lived in peace during his lifetime. He lived a very long time, just as his brother Siv. His spirit resides on this plane in the forests of Myrkwood among his companions, the creatures of those forests. He may have information that will help you upon this journey. He can be found among the creatures of [Myrkwood]. Seek out Coplin's Spirit! Return to me when you have finished. I cannot believe I hold all but the last piece of the crest! You have done wonders my friend! We have only to merge the five piece into one and [fulfill the wish] of a fallen king, now kept for hundreds of years. The crest pieces can only be merged in the fires of a [forge within Muspelheim]. It is our hopes that should be this accomplished, Svan Alfevson will hear our calling and deliver unto us the final piece. Take these four pieces and seek out the dverge fire-eaters within Muspelheim. They may distrust you at first, but I am told they hate the fire giants that also walk within the fire realm. If you are able to make into the forge of five anvils, deliver all four piece to one named Sinyr. He will do his best to fashion the Grenlock [crest pieces] into one. If the last of the five piece are delivered unto you, Sinyr will make the crest while once more. I look forward to your return! You champion our cause, and we are honored you have taken on this task.
